key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose where photoelectrochemical cell losses occur and turn that diagnosis into actionable design guidance across both BIJ and SEJ device architectures.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers compare materials, quantify efficiency limits, and prioritize fixes such as improving light absorption, reducing recombination, or upgrading interfacial catalysis.
method: Fits experimental current-voltage curves with physically meaningful loss terms
Decomposes losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial contributions
Uses efficiency maps and Sankey diagrams to visualize limits and energy flow
evidence_signal: The model is validated against literature results spanning solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of experimental fitting and the chosen physical assumptions, so parameter extraction may be sensitive to noisy or incomplete current-voltage data.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
